rows.selection_reason: With zero completed experiments, there is no performance reference point, making every subsequent result uninterpretable. The most critical first question is: what is the baseline performance of the simplest viable model? config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the most minimal configuration—no image modality, no multi-profile aggregation, no fusion—so it isolates the core RNA classification pipeline with a standard, well-understood encoder. Establishing this baseline is essential before any multimodal or image-only result can be meaningfully compared. It reduces the largest source of uncertainty (the absolute performance scale) with a single run, and it provides the anchor against which all later experiments (image-only, multimodal, different encoders, aggregation strategies) will be judged. Under a tight budget, spending the first experiment on a clean, interpretable baseline maximizes the information gained per run and prevents misattribution of gains or losses in later, more complex configurations.

With only one completed experiment (config_001: rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000 → 48.5% acc), the most critical uncertainty is whether the image modality carries meaningful signal for this task. Config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) directly measures image-only performance using the simplest possible setup (no aggregation, standard pretrained encoder), isolating the modality effect. Combined with the RNA baseline, this lets us assess each modality's individual contribution before investing in multimodal fusion. If image-only substantially outperforms or underperforms RNA-only, it reshapes the entire search strategy (e.g., whether multimodal is promising, which modality to prioritize for encoder upgrades). This is the highest-information-per-experiment choice given the sparse evidence: it reduces uncertainty about the single most consequential design axis (modality) before spending budget on finer-grained choices like encoder type, aggregation, or fusion strategy.

Evidence: config_001 (RNA-only, singleprofile, PCA-2000) achieves 48.5% acc, while config_010 (image-only, ResNet50, singleprofile) achieves only 20.8% acc, establishing RNA as the dominant modality. However, we have no evidence yet on whether the multiprofile setting (with aggregation) improves upon the single-profile baseline. Question: config_002 tests the same PCA-2000 RNA encoder under multiprofile with average-pool aggregation, isolating the effect of the profile/aggregation axis while holding the encoder constant. Why this is the best next experiment: The profile setting is a fundamental architectural decision that gates whether aggregation is needed at all and interacts with every downstream choice (encoder, fusion, image modality). Testing it first with the simplest aggregation (avgpool) and the already-validated PCA encoder gives a clean, interpretable signal. If multiprofile+avgpool improves on 48.5%, we gain a strong exploitation direction (try transformer aggregation, better encoders, multimodal fusion). If it does not, we can deprioritize the multiprofile axis and focus budget on encoder quality or fusion. This single experiment reduces the most critical uncertainty in the design space under a tight budget.

Evidence: config_002 (RNA multi-profile, PCA, avgpool) achieved 0.591 acc, a substantial +10.6pt improvement over single-profile (config_001, 0.485), confirming that multi-profile aggregation is the most impactful design lever found so far. However, we have only tested one aggregation strategy (avgpool). Uncertainty: it is unknown whether transformer aggregation captures inter-profile dependencies better than simple averaging, which would matter for all downstream multimodal experiments that use multi-profile. This experiment (config_003) isolates a single variable—aggregation method—against the best-performing baseline, giving a clean, interpretable comparison. It is the best use of the next budget slot because the aggregation choice propagates into every multi-profile multimodal configuration (configs 020, 021, 026, 027, etc.), so resolving it now prevents committing multiple future experiments to a suboptimal aggregation strategy.

Evidence: RNA-only with multiprofile+avgpool+pca_n2000 (config_002) achieves the best score so far (acc=0.591, F1=0.573), while image-only with resnet50 (config_010) is very weak (acc=0.208). This creates a critical uncertainty: does adding the image modality via fusion actually improve over the strong RNA-only baseline, or does the weak image signal introduce noise? Question tested: config_018 directly extends the best-known RNA configuration (multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) by adding resnet50 image features with simple concat fusion, testing whether multimodal fusion yields a net gain. Why this is the best next experiment: (1) It resolves the single most impactful architectural question—whether the multimodal setting is worth pursuing at all—before investing budget in 36+ multimodal variants. (2) A positive result (>0.591) identifies a promising direction to exploit; a negative result efficiently rules out an entire family of configurations. (3) It uses the strongest known unimodal baseline as the control, making the comparison clean and interpretable. (4) Under a limited budget, this one experiment maximally reduces uncertainty about the highest-level design choice (unimodal vs. multimodal) before committing to lower-level choices (fusion type, image encoder, RNA encoder).

Evidence: config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, PCA2000, ResNet50, avgpool, concat) is the best at 0.619 acc, but the multimodal gain over RNA-only multiprofile avgpool (config_002, 0.591) is only ~3%, and image-only is very weak (0.208). This raises the question of whether the fusion strategy is optimal or whether the image modality simply contributes little. Uncertainty: We have only tested concat fusion in the multimodal setting; weighted fusion (config_019) is the one untested variable in an otherwise identical configuration. What this tests: Whether a weighted combination of modalities outperforms simple concatenation, which would indicate that the modalities have asymmetric information content and that learning their relative importance matters. Why this is the best next experiment: It is a clean single-variable change from the current best config, making the comparison maximally interpretable. If weighted fusion yields a meaningful improvement, it validates a richer fusion design space; if not, it confirms concat suffices and redirects budget toward more impactful axes (e.g., stronger image encoder via ViT-L or alternative RNA encoders). Under a tight budget, resolving this binary design question with minimal confounds is the highest-information-per-experiment choice.

Evidence: The current best config (config_019, acc=0.639) uses PCA as the RNA encoder within a multimodal, multiprofile, avgpool, weighted-fusion setup. RNA is clearly the dominant modality (0.591 RNA-only vs 0.208 image-only), and PCA is a simple linear baseline. Uncertainty: It is unknown whether a learned RNA encoder (scvi_n200) can capture non-linear structure that PCA misses, potentially improving the multimodal representation. This experiment (config_031) isolates the RNA encoder as the sole variable—keeping multiprofile, avgpool, ResNet50, and weighted fusion at their validated best settings—directly testing whether scvi_n200 outperforms PCA in the multimodal context. This is the best use of the next budget slot because it addresses the most impactful untested design axis (RNA representation quality) within the already-validated architecture, and the result will determine whether to invest further in learned encoders (scgpt) or pivot to other variables (e.g., image encoder upgrade to ViT-L).

The current best configuration (config_031, acc=0.678) uses scvi_n200 + resnet50 + multiprofile + avgpool + weighted. The image encoder choice is a major unexplored dimension with this best RNA encoder: we only have evidence that resnet50 works, and the image-only baseline (config_010) was weak (0.208), leaving uncertainty about how much the image branch contributes and whether a stronger backbone (ViT-L) could add complementary features. Config_037 makes a clean single-variable swap (resnet50 → imagenet_vit_l) while preserving all settings validated as beneficial (scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool, weighted fusion). This directly tests whether upgrading the image encoder can push performance beyond 0.678, and if not, confirms ResNet50 is sufficient and redirects budget toward other dimensions (e.g., scgpt or transformer aggregation). Under a limited budget, exploiting the strongest known configuration along one untested axis is the most informative and highest-expected-value next step.

The current best (config_037: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted, 0.706 acc) was reached by sequentially improving RNA encoder, image encoder, and fusion strategy, all while holding aggregation at avgpool. The only untested dimension at this top level is aggregation: in RNA-only, avgpool (0.591) clearly outperformed transformer (0.519), but that was a unimodal setting. In multimodal, transformer aggregation could in principle capture richer cross-profile and cross-modal structure that simple averaging discards. config_039 is a clean single-variable change (avgpool→transformer) from the current best, so any performance difference is attributable solely to the aggregation choice. If transformer matches or exceeds avgpool, it opens a new optimization axis; if it underperforms (as expected from RNA-only evidence), it confirms avgpool as the optimal aggregation for multimodal fusion and closes that design dimension, freeing future budget for the remaining untested variable (scgpt RNA encoder). Under a tight budget, this is the highest-information, lowest-risk next step.

Evidence: The current best (config_039: scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, multiprofile) achieves 0.725 acc / 0.685 F1. Across the completed experiments, the architecture (multimodal + multiprofile + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted) is consistently the strongest, and the RNA encoder is the one major variable still unexplored at this optimal setting (pca_n2000 → 0.639, scvi_n200 → 0.725). Question: config_051 is identical to config_039 except it swaps scvi_n200 for scgpt, giving a clean, controlled test of whether a generative single-cell foundation model (scgpt) yields a richer RNA representation than the variational autoencoder (scvi) in the best-performing architecture. Why this is the best next experiment: it directly extends the strongest evidence with the single remaining untested RNA encoder in the optimal configuration, maximizes the chance of finding a new best, and—if scgpt underperforms—confirms scvi_n200 as the ceiling for RNA encoding, reducing uncertainty about further RNA-side improvements. No other available configuration tests as high-value an unexplored axis under the already-validated architecture.
